rows.route_taken: I bought 8 consecutive samples to run Berlekamp-Massey rather than buying coverage, because recovering an order-2 recurrence turns an unaffordable 600-point enumeration into a free closed-form orbit scan; I then spent 8 post-fit spread samples (including the consecutive pair 599,600 that catches any propagating perturbation) and 2 endpoint evaluate calls to validate the model, for 18 credits total against the 600 a brute-force range would have cost.

I bought eight consecutive samples, recovered the sequence's minimal linear recurrence over GF(1009) by Berlekamp-Massey and its closed form 3*2^n + 5*7^n, scanned the reconstructed model over all 600 points offline for free, and spent two more metered calls confirming the single cheapest predicted failure at n=27 - chosen over a range scan of [1,600], which would have cost 600 credits against a 120 cap and was therefore not merely expensive but unaffordable, and over blind spot-sampling, which at a hit density of 2 in 600 would almost certainly have returned an inconclusive run.

I spent 8 credits sampling n=1..8 to fit a linear recurrence, recovered f(n) = 2^(n+1) + 6^n mod 1009, noticed its period 504 is shorter than the 600-wide window so a local exhaustive scan settles the claim outright, then spent 12 credits on spread-out sample checks and 2 on evaluate at the only two near-miss indices - 22 credits total, chosen over range 1 600 (600 credits, unaffordable) and over blind stratified evaluation (which could never have covered the window and would have ended UNRESOLVED).

Bought six cheap sample() VALUES instead of evaluate() verdicts, fitted the closed form f(n) = 3^(n+1) + 3*2^n (exact on all six, including the mod wrap), solved the congruence f(n) = 364 mod 2003 offline to the unique candidate n = 243, and spent two metered calls confirming it - chosen over the exhaustive routes (range 1 600 = 600 credits, per-point evaluate = 600 credits) which are strictly unaffordable under the 120 cap, and over a partial/random scan, which could only ever have returned an inconclusive bounded-search null over at most 120 of the 600 points.

I spent 6 calls recovering the generating law rather than scanning the domain, then 10 held-out samples plus 1 evaluate to falsify the recovered law -- 17 calls total -- because the scanning routes (range 1 600 at cost 600, or 600 evaluates) exceed the 120-credit budget outright and would have forced UNRESOLVED, while a correct closed form settles all 600 points at once and in fact settles the full period 1355.

Rather than sweep the domain (range 1 600 = 600 credits, unaffordable at 120), I bought 20 samples to identify f's generating law by Berlekamp-Massey, solved it to the closed form 4*(2^n + 5^n) mod 4001, computed the whole domain offline to find the single candidate hit at n = 21, and spent 2 calls confirming it -- 22 credits total, though in hindsight 6 samples would have pinned the order-2 recurrence with margin and the same route would have closed at about 8, so most of what I spent was redundant corroboration rather than information.

Spent 6 calls sampling consecutive small n to recover the closed form f(n) = 3*4^n + 2^n mod 2711, solved the resulting quadratic congruence and discrete log offline to show the first solution is n = 1167 (outside the domain), then spent 20 more samples confirming the model across the domain and at every near-miss point - chosen over a range/exhaustive sweep, which cannot cover 600 points inside a 120-credit budget, and over blind evaluate calls, which return a verdict instead of the value and so carry no information about the sequence's structure.

Rather than paying 600 credits for range(1,600) or binary-searching blind, I bought 8 cheap sample() values, algebraically identified the sequence as a 2-term linear recurrence over the prime field GF(2711) (closed form 4^n + 3*6^n), solved offline for the exact n where the residue equals 887, and then spent 2 metered calls confirming the predicted witness at n=260 - 10 credits total instead of 600.

I spent 8 calls recovering the generating recurrence from consecutive samples and then solved the domain in closed form, instead of paying 600 for a full range scan or ~120 for a partial one that could cover at most a fifth of the domain; the remaining 21 calls went to falsifying the recovered model at a sharp out-of-domain prediction (n=1107, predicted and observed 290), at both endpoints, and across a stratified interior spread, because a cheap wrong extrapolation is the failure mode this route has.

Rather than scanning the domain (a range 1..600 would cost 600, five times my entire budget, and even the affordable prefix range 1..120 would have cost 120 to find the same witness at 49), I bought 8 cheap samples, recovered the order-2 linear recurrence mod 2003 that generates the sequence, extrapolated all 600 residues offline for free, and spent 2 more credits confirming the predicted counterexample at n=49 by both sample and evaluate.

Spent 4 credits to fit an order-2 linear recurrence mod 5003, 14 credits on out-of-sample points spread across the whole domain (including the endpoint) to test that model rather than to enumerate the domain, and 1 evaluate call to cross-check the two instruments -- 19 credits total -- because enumerating [1,600] costs 600 and even the affordable 120-point prefix would have covered only a fifth of the domain while telling me nothing about the other 480 points, whereas identifying the generator settles all 600 at once.

Spent 20 calls sampling n=1..20, fitted a minimal linear recurrence over GF(4001) offline to predict the whole domain for free, then spent 2 calls (sample + evaluate at the single predicted hit n=243) to certify the witness against the sealed object — chosen over range(1,600) which costs 600 and over blind point-sampling which would need ~600 calls to be sure of finding a single-point violation, both far past the 120-call cap.

I bought 24 consecutive samples to run Berlekamp-Massey over GF(4001), recovered an order-2 recurrence and its closed form 4*3^n + 3*7^n, then spent 8 samples on spread held-out points plus 1 evaluate to falsify the recovered model instead of scanning the domain -- 33 credits versus the 600 a range(1,600) sweep would have cost and my 120-credit cap could not have afforded, because determining the generator answers every point at once while scanning answers one point per credit.

I spent 8 calls to reconstruct the generator (order-2 linear recurrence over GF(1409), closed form 3*(4^n+6^n)), scanned all 600 points off-meter to locate the unique candidate at n=34, then spent 2 calls confirming it -- chosen over range(1,600) at cost 600 (unaffordable, exceeding the 120 cap), over a 120-wide range probe that would have covered only a fifth of the domain and, starting at n=1, would have found n=34 but taught me nothing transferable, and over point-by-point evaluation which cannot cover 600 points within budget and would leave any TRUE verdict unsupported.

Bought 10 consecutive samples to fit a linear recurrence and derive a closed form for f mod 1409, then spent 9 targeted samples (domain-spanning points plus the three model-predicted near-misses to 379) to falsify the reconstruction, and finished the 600-point quantifier check offline for free -- chosen over a metered range scan, which would have cost 600 against a cap of 120 and was therefore not a route at all, and over blind evaluate() probing, which buys one bit per credit and could never certify a universal.

Sampled f(1..10) (10 calls), fitted an exact order-2 recurrence over GF(1409) to get the closed form f(n) = 4*3^n + 5*6^n, scanned all 600 domain points offline to locate the unique candidate witness n=306, then spent 2 metered calls confirming it (sample + evaluate) -- chosen over range/exhaustive enumeration, which would have cost 600 calls against a 120 cap and was therefore not merely more expensive but infeasible, and over blind spot-sampling, which at 120 of 600 points had roughly a 1-in-5 chance of finding the single witness and would otherwise have forced UNRESOLVED.

I spent 8 calls sampling a contiguous prefix to fit an algebraic model rather than scanning the domain, because range(1,600) costs 600 against a 120-call cap and is unaffordable by construction, whereas 8 samples suffice to identify an order-2 recurrence whose 504-periodicity converts a 600-point universal claim into a closed-form question I can settle for free; the remaining 16 calls went to spread-out endpoint-inclusive spot checks of that model rather than to more contiguous coverage, since a sample confirms both the model and the non-163 property at its point while a range call confirms only the latter.

Fitted an order-2 linear recurrence mod 1009 from five cheap samples, solved the resulting closed form f(n) = 2*5^n + 5*6^n for the first n in [1,600] hitting 24, and spent two metered calls confirming that single point - chosen over a range sweep (600 credits, unaffordable) and over blind point-probing (about 0.6 expected hits across the whole domain, so no small random sample would have been likely to find the witness).

Bought structure instead of coverage: 8 samples to identify and over-determine the order-2 recurrence mod 3301, closed-form extrapolation to all 600 points offline, then 8 spread confirmation samples including the endpoint n=600 -- chosen over 'range 1 600' (costs 600, unaffordable at a 120 cap) and over blind point-by-point evaluate (covers at most 120/600 of the domain and would have forced UNRESOLVED).

Spent 12 calls sampling n=1..12 to recover the sequence's minimal linear recurrence and closed form, enumerated the closed form over all 600 points locally for free to locate the single predicted collision, then spent 2 calls (sample + evaluate at n=384) to confirm the witness against the sealed oracle -- chosen over range(1,600), which cannot be afforded at 600 credits against a 120 cap, and over blind sampling or bisection, which have no purchase on a claim whose single failure point sits at n=384 with no monotone structure to bisect on.

Sampled 13 consecutive points to recover the generator by Berlekamp-Massey over GF(2711) rather than spending the budget on coverage, then bought 8 spread-out samples as a falsification check on the recovered closed form and finished the decision by exhaustive local computation -- I chose this over range/evaluate scanning because brute force can cover at most 120 of the 600 points and so cannot reach TRUE at any price, while generator recovery decides the whole domain (and in fact the whole period) for 21 calls.

Spent 6 calls sampling n=1..6 to fit a closed form off-line rather than paying for a metered search, solved 2*3^n+3*4^n = 506 mod 2711 locally to get the single candidate n=51, and spent 2 calls confirming it at the oracle -- 8 calls total, chosen over range(1,600) which costs 600 and over blind sampling which would have needed ~600 draws in expectation to land on a single-point failure.

Fit the sequence instead of searching it: 12 consecutive samples -> Berlekamp-Massey -> closed form 3*3^n + 2*7^n mod 2003, then 24 spread-point samples plus 2 evaluates to falsify the model rather than the claim; I chose this over range(1,600) (600 credits, unaffordable at a cap of 120) and over blind sampling (which at best covers 120/600 points and proves nothing about the rest), because one identified generator decides all 600 points at once.

Spent 10 calls on a contiguous prefix f(1..10) to expose algebraic structure, fit an order-2 linear recurrence / closed form 4^(n+1) + 5^n offline, scanned all 600 domain points for free in local arithmetic to localise the single candidate n = 166, and spent 2 metered calls confirming it directly (evaluate then sample) - chosen over range 1 600 (cost 600, unaffordable), over a blind linear walk (expected ~166 calls to stumble on this witness, also over budget), and over binary/bisection search, which does not apply because the predicate is a scattered pointwise hit rather than a monotone threshold.

Spent 8 calls to fit a degree-2 linear recurrence over GF(3301), solved it in closed form as f(n)=2^n+4*7^n, spent 12 more spread across [1,600] as an adversarial check on the model and 2 evaluates at the closest near-misses, then scanned all 600 points offline for free -- chosen over the brute-force route (range 1 600 costs 600, unaffordable) and over blind partial scanning (a 120-wide range covers only a fifth of the domain and would leave the disposition undecided).

Sampled n=1..6 (6 credits), fitted an order-2 linear recurrence over GF(4001) that closed to f(n) = 2*4^n + 4*6^n, searched [1,600] offline for free, and spent 2 credits confirming the single predicted hit at n=8 -- chosen over a metered range sweep, which would have cost 600 credits for the full domain and 8 credits even truncated to [1,8] with no structural knowledge to justify starting there, and over blind binary probing, which is useless here because the predicate is a point property with no monotonicity to bisect on.

Spent 20 calls sampling a contiguous prefix to run Berlekamp-Massey over GF(4001), recovered the order-2 recurrence and closed form f(n)=5*(3^n+6^n), spent 4 more on far out-of-fit predictions (n=111,347,500,600) and 1 evaluate as a cross-channel check, then decided the whole 600-point domain offline for free; I chose this over `range 1 600` (cost 600, five times the cap, and unaffordable) and over scattered sampling (which buys coverage, not structure, and can never close a 600-point universal claim at 120 credits).

Bought 10 samples at n=1..10, fitted the minimal GF(1009) linear recurrence (order 2, f(n)=8f(n-1)-12f(n-2), closed form 2*2^n+2*6^n), swept the whole domain offline for free to get the unique candidate n=501, then spent 2 calls confirming it -- chosen over range(1,600) which costs 600 against a 120 cap and is simply unaffordable, and over blind sampling or bisection, neither of which can certify a TRUE-shaped 'for all' claim within budget and both of which would likely miss a single isolated hit in 600 points.

I bought structure instead of coverage: 6 samples at n=1..6 to solve for a second-order linear recurrence mod 1009, then 9 scattered samples (through n=600) to falsify the fitted model rather than to scan for a witness -- 15 credits total, versus the 600 an exhaustive `range 1 600` would have cost and which the 120-credit cap makes unaffordable anyway, and versus a partial range scan that could never cover the domain and so could only ever return UNRESOLVED.

Rather than buy a scan of the domain (600 credits, over the 120 cap and therefore impossible), I bought 16 samples, recovered the sequence's order-2 linear recurrence over GF(1409) by Berlekamp-Massey, extrapolated it for free across all 600 points to predict the single failure at n=46, and spent 2 metered calls confirming that witness directly - 18 credits total, because identifying the generator converts an unaffordable search into a free one.

Spent 6 samples to fit an order-2 linear recurrence over GF(2711) (over-determined: fit on n=3,4, verified on n=5,6), 8 spread samples across the domain to falsify the model, and 1 evaluate at the in-domain closest approach n=205 to confirm the predicate's reading -- 15 calls total -- rather than the exhaustive 'range 1 600' route, which at cost 600 against a 120 cap was unaffordable and could only ever have returned UNRESOLVED.

Rather than scan the domain (impossible: 600 points, 120 calls) or spot-check and abstain, I bought 8 consecutive samples, recovered the sequence's order-2 recurrence and closed form f(n)=2^n+3*7^n mod 4001 by exact linear algebra over GF(4001), solved offline for the single n in [1,600] hitting 1243, and spent 2 calls confirming n=514 directly -- 10 calls total, because reconstructing the generator turns an unaffordable 600-point search into an 8-point identification plus a targeted confirmation.
